pages.text:
Quincy Miller has spent twenty-two years in prison for a murder he insists he did not commit. A letter brings his case to Cullen Post, a lawyer and minister who works to overturn wrongful convictions. Investigating the killing of a Florida lawyer, Post finds people with powerful reasons to keep the verdict intact.

John Grisham builds this legal thriller around the work of returning to old evidence and challenging an apparently settled case. The danger grows as the search for justice threatens those who benefited from Miller’s imprisonment.

Bruenor sets out to reclaim Mithral Hall, the dwarven home his people lost long ago. Drizzt Do’Urden, Wulfgar and Regis join him on a journey through dangerous country, where friendship must withstand threats that none of them could face as easily alone.

The second Icewind Dale novel continues the adventures begun in The Crystal Shard. R. A. Salvatore combines a quest for a lost homeland with Drizzt’s struggle between the pull of his past in the Underdark and the loyalties he has formed on the surface.

pages.text:
Jake Howard’s wealth and success seem perfectly matched by his wife Helen’s beauty and intelligence. Yet their marriage depends on appearances and assumptions that leave little room for either person to be understood. As attraction begins to disturb that arrangement, each must look beyond the role assigned to the other.

Anne Mather’s romance explores the distance between an outwardly enviable marriage and the feelings concealed inside it. Helen’s resistance to being treated as a possession challenges Jake’s expectations and makes their future together uncertain.

Caitlin’s marriage to Monro Ritchie looks fortunate from the outside: an attractive husband and a luxurious life seem to leave little wanting. Privately, she knows how empty their relationship has become. Just as she begins to understand her feelings for him, something from her past puts further strain on their bond.

Charlotte Lamb centres this romance on the gap between material comfort and emotional trust. Caitlin must confront the possibility that an apparently successful marriage may still fail, and decide whether the distance between them can be overcome.

An inherited cottage gives Claire Richards and her daughter Lucy a chance to live independently. Lucy’s friendship with Jay Fraser’s daughter brings the families together, although Jay initially distrusts Claire’s intentions. When storm damage makes the cottage uninhabitable, accepting his help changes their relationship.

Penny Jordan follows a marriage proposed for practical reasons into less manageable emotional territory. Claire hopes to give Lucy security, but living alongside Jay reveals a different man from the one she first encountered and makes a loveless arrangement increasingly difficult to accept.

After her mother’s death, Amy must help keep the Heartland horse rehabilitation farm running while struggling with her own grief. Caring for frightened horses demands patience and trust at a time when the people around them also need to heal. Spartan’s return and Pegasus’s failing health make that responsibility increasingly personal.

This omnibus contains the first three Heartland stories: Coming Home, After the Storm and Breaking Free. Lauren Brooke connects the work of caring for animals with family loss, growing independence and learning to continue another person’s legacy.

pages.text:
Phoebe remembers her brother Mick as mischievous, funny and impossible to replace. After he dies in a bicycle accident, familiar memories become both a comfort and a source of pain. Neither her family nor her friends find an easy way to respond to the space he has left behind.

Barbara Park tells this short novel through a sister trying to make sense of sudden loss. Humorous recollections preserve Mick’s personality while Phoebe’s account explores grief, guilt and the difficulty of continuing ordinary life after a death.

pages.text:
Anthony Vidler examines how streets, institutions and architectural ideas have shaped the modern city. The opening essay follows changes in urban reality from 1750 to 1871; the collection then moves through questions of transparency, public monuments, libraries, industrial communities and utopian planning.

Studies of figures including Tony Garnier, Le Corbusier and Guy Debord connect the design of physical space with political and cultural ambitions. This is architectural criticism and history, offering several ways to read a city rather than a single set of instructions for designing one.

pages.text:
Dolores Price recounts a life shaped by painful experiences, loneliness and the wish to be loved. As a teenager she retreats into television and food, but growing older brings further encounters that challenge the ways she has learned to protect herself. Her voice mixes sharp humour with a deeply wounded view of the world.

Wally Lamb follows Dolores from childhood into adulthood in a novel about damage and the difficult work of starting again. Relationships, self-image and the possibility of trust remain central to her search for a life she can inhabit.

Hans-Erik Petermann introduceert jiujitsu aan de hand van de geschiedenis en de technische opbouw van de vechtkunst. Hij bespreekt onder meer voetenwerk, verdediging, trappen, worpen, klemmen en grondtechnieken. Ook Braziliaans jiujitsu krijgt een plaats in het overzicht.

De geïllustreerde gids brengt verschillende onderdelen van training en zelfverdediging bij elkaar, zodat de lezer hun onderlinge samenhang kan zien. Het boek richt zich zowel op geïnteresseerde beginners als op mensen die al trainen en een beknopte uitleg van de achtergrond en basiselementen zoeken.

Slappy is used to frightening other people, but ventriloquist Jimmy O’James has acquired another dummy that looks exactly like him. The newcomer arrives with instructions that threaten Slappy’s own future. Facing a double turns the familiar menace of the living dummy into a more personal nightmare.

pages.text:
Rosalyn Schanzer places George Washington and Britain’s King George III alongside one another to explain the American Revolution from opposing viewpoints. Their lives and positions introduce the larger disagreement between the colonies and the government that claimed authority over them.

Illustrations and historical accounts help younger readers follow the growth of conflict, including disputes over taxation and representation. The comparison encourages readers to consider why the same events could look different to each side, rather than treating the war as a contest between an uncomplicated hero and villain.

Waar de gezamenlijke verontwaardiging duidelijk lijkt, blijkt opkomen voor iemand dichtbij minder vanzelfsprekend.

pages.beforeSynopsis: De beschrijving wordt geladen. Beschrijving van een therapeutische methode waarbij het herstel van het spanningsevenwicht in het lichaam centraal staat bij de behandeling van psychische problemen
pages.text:
Ad Stemerding beschrijft een lichaamsgerichte benadering van psychotherapie waarin spanning, beweging en gevoelsbeleving samen worden bekeken. Vanuit zijn opvatting van therapie als groeiproces bespreekt hij onderwerpen als vertrouwen, identiteit, emotionele expressie en zelfbepaling. Ook houding, ademhaling en ontspanning krijgen aandacht.

Deze uitgave uit 1981 geeft inzicht in de begrippen en werkwijzen van de auteur binnen die benadering. De nadruk ligt op zijn ideeën over samenhang tussen lichaam en psychische ervaringen. Het boek kan worden gelezen als een historische uiteenzetting van lichaamsgerichte therapie, zonder de beschreven opvattingen als actuele medische conclusies te behandelen.

work.description:
**Egalia’s Daughters** (original title: *Egalias døtre*) is a novel by Gerd Brantenberg that was first published in 1977 in Norwegian. The novel is like most of Brantenberg's other work norm-breaking in such a way that it questions the social, existential and erotic position of women in the society. The book has been translated into several languages and is considered a feminist literature classic.

The name of the former feminist community Megalia was based partly on the name of this book.

(Source: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egalia%27s_Daughters))

pages.sourceName: Open Library — exact edition and book-jacket description
pages.text:
In Egalia, women hold public power while men are expected to organise their lives around domestic responsibilities. Even everyday language reinforces that division: the ruling group are called wim, and menwim occupy the subordinate position. What inhabitants regard as ordinary begins to look less inevitable when those expectations are questioned.

Gerd Brantenberg uses an invented society to examine familiar patterns of authority and dependence. Reversing gender roles makes social conventions newly visible, while the satire asks how power shapes behaviour regardless of who happens to possess it.

pages.text:
Ben takes a short walk behind his hotel during a business trip to Pennsylvania. Once in the woods, he discovers that getting back is no longer a matter of retracing his steps. The path draws him into a strange world whose creatures and rules turn an ordinary afternoon into a fight to return to his family.

Drew Magary mixes a dangerous quest with absurd humour and the unpredictability of a nightmare. Folk-tale and video-game elements shape Ben’s journey, while the life he left behind gives the adventure its personal stakes.

pages.text:
Koning Edward II geeft zijn minnaar Gaveston een positie die de gevestigde adel niet wil aanvaarden. Zijn keuze brengt persoonlijke liefde en openbaar gezag met elkaar in botsing. Binnen het hof en de koninklijke familie groeit het verzet, waardoor de strijd om invloed steeds gewelddadiger wordt.

Tom Lanoye bewerkt Christopher Marlowes koningsdrama tot een Nederlandstalige toneeltekst waarin macht, afkomst en begeerte door elkaar lopen. De tragikomische benadering laat zien hoe een intieme verhouding een politieke crisis kan ontketenen en hoe snel verdedigers van traditie zelf naar de kroon grijpen.

pages.author: Michiel Stroink

pages.beforeSynopsis:
De beschrijving wordt geladen. Max, een dertigjarige pokerprofessional, leeft en werkt volgens een strak geordend schema. Met zijn 'tien dagen op en tien dagen af'-systeem, waarin hij zich op de been houdt met veel drank en drugs, hoopt hij aan de pokertafel zo snel mogelijk miljonair te worden.
Maar zijn plan wordt in de war geschopt als hij wordt geveld door acuut leverfalen. Hij belandt in het ziekenhuis, waar al snel duidelijk wordt dat hij door zijn exorbitante levensstijl geen recht heeft op de noodzakelijke transplantatie.
Max dreigt de controle over zijn leven te verliezen en probeert zichzelf te redden op de enige manier die hij kent: door te pokeren, maar dan met de mensen in zijn directe omgeving als speelkaarten. Er ontstaat een intrigerend machtsspel, met het leven van Max als inzet.
pages.text:
Pokerprofessional Max probeert zijn leven net zo precies te beheersen als een spel. Tien dagen spelen worden gevolgd door tien dagen herstel, terwijl drank en drugs hem op de been houden. Wanneer hij met ernstige leverschade in het ziekenhuis belandt, bieden zijn berekeningen geen uitweg meer.

Michiel Stroink verplaatst de spanning van de pokertafel naar de vraag hoeveel invloed iemand op zijn eigen overleven heeft. Een verpleegkundige probeert Max te helpen, maar zijn afhankelijkheid van anderen botst met de overtuiging dat hij iedere situatie zelf kan sturen.

pages.author: Léon Krier

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Loading the description. Provides a contemporary road map for designing or completing the fragmented communities of today. Illustrated throughout with original drawings, explains theories on classical and vernacular urbanism and architecture, while providing practical design guidelines for creating livable towns.
Includes drawings, diagrams, and photographs of built works by Krier, which have not been widely seen until now. From publisher description.
pages.sourceName: Island Press — catalogue via University of Toronto Press Distribution
pages.text:
Léon Krier sets out his approach to designing towns and cities around human use, drawing on classical and vernacular building traditions. Drawings, diagrams and examples of built work explain how streets, buildings and public spaces can form coherent communities.

The book revises and expands ideas from Architecture: Choice or Fate. Krier combines criticism of prevailing planning practices with practical design proposals, making his argument visible through illustrations as well as prose. It offers a particular architectural vision of livable settlements and the choices that give them their character.

John Bratton introduces the study of behaviour at work by connecting organisational theory with the experience of people inside organisations. This third edition considers managerial and critical perspectives together, with particular attention to ethics, diversity and the international settings in which work takes place.

edition.description:
No one writes about modern India like Daksh Tyagi.

Inspired by true stories, Daksh Tyagi's witty and hugely entertaining book 'A Nation of Idiots' takes on the uncomfortable, the unsettling, and the often misunderstood modern Indian life. This polarising and provocative Indian bestseller fences with terribly tricky social, moral, and cultural dilemmas facing modern Indians, as it makes sense of one of the world’s most complex societies.


WE INDIANS ARE AN INTERESTING BUNCH.
Intolerant to the debate on intolerance, but tolerant of religious intolerance. We cling onto age-old traditions, but a holiday can alter our accent. To us, caste and community is a badge of trust, religion is a line of control and a godman is an anti-depressant.
We won’t stop at a zebra crossing, but we will damn well stop on it. We build things to prove our worth and break things to prove a point. We love the concept of independence, but we need our parents to help raise our kids. And we scripted the Kamasutra. Easy to forget, since we also ruined sex.
So how do we tell the real from the farcical? The farcical from the nutty? And the nutty from the downright ridiculous?
Easy. We just go along.

Daksh Tyagi's funny and insightful 'A Nation of Idiots' is the ideal guide to surviving the modern Indian life with your scruples intact.

Daksh Tyagi examines the contradictions of modern Indian life through humour and stories inspired by real situations. Religious boundaries, caste, family dependence and public behaviour become ways of asking why people’s stated values can diverge from their everyday choices.

The book approaches social and moral dilemmas through satire rather than offering a neutral catalogue of national customs. Tyagi’s observations invite readers to recognise familiar evasions and inconsistencies, and to consider how inherited expectations can survive alongside the language of independence, progress and tolerance.

pages.text:
Joris Luyendijk onderzoekt hoe zijn eigen achtergrond hem toegang gaf tot posities waarin mensen zoals hij de norm bepalen. Hij kijkt naar zeven kenmerken rond gezin, afkomst, huidskleur, geslacht, seksuele identiteit en opleiding. Juist wie op al die punten voordeel heeft, kan volgens hem moeilijk aanvoelen hoe uitsluiting werkt.

pages.text:
Private investigator Cormoran Strike is struggling financially and living with the consequences of losing a leg in Afghanistan. A new client asks him to investigate the death of supermodel Lula Landry, which the police have treated as suicide. Following her final movements takes Strike into a London world of wealth, celebrity and carefully guarded appearances.

Robert Galbraith introduces a detective whose own circumstances contrast sharply with the people he questions. The investigation depends on looking beyond public images and testing the stories told by those closest to the dead woman.

pages.text:
In 2010 vertrekt Geert Mak vanaf het huis waar John Steinbeck vijftig jaar eerder aan zijn reis door Amerika begon. Hij volgt diens spoor door steden en dorpen en vraagt wat er van de verwachtingen van toen is terechtgekomen. Ontmoetingen onderweg verbinden het dagelijks leven met de grotere geschiedenis van het land.

Mak combineert reisverslag en historische beschouwing om veranderingen in de Amerikaanse samenleving te onderzoeken. Ook de verhouding met Europa krijgt aandacht. De vergelijking tussen 1960 en 2010 vormt het raamwerk van deze zoektocht naar een land achter zijn bekende beelden.

De familie Talamini leeft tussen de Italiaanse bergen en een ijssalon in Rotterdam. Voor vader Giuseppe hoort het ambacht bij een traditie die zijn zonen moeten voortzetten. Giovanni kiest echter voor de poëzie en bouwt een bestaan buiten het familiebedrijf op. Een onverwacht verzoek van zijn broer Luca brengt die keuze opnieuw aan het wankelen.

Ernest van der Kwast verbindt het maken van ijs met verhalen over verschillende generaties. De roman draait om familieverplichtingen, persoonlijke vrijheid en de vraag hoeveel afstand iemand kan nemen van een afkomst die hem tegelijk blijft vormen.

description.value:
"We live, says Ed Schein, in a culture of Tell. Rather than trying to genuinely relate to other people we tell them what we think they need to know or should do based on assumptions we've made about them. But telling makes people feel inferior--it shuts them down. This is particularly true of interactions between superiors and subordinates, and that's where it's particularly problematic. In today's complex, interconnected, rapidly changing world hierarchy means nothing--anybody anywhere could have that vital fact or insight that could mean the difference between success or disaster. A free flow of information is crucial. Humble Inquiry builds the kinds of positive, trusting, balanced relationships that encourage honest and open interactions in both our professional and personal lives. Schein defines Humble Inquiry as "the fine art of drawing someone out, of asking questions to which you do not know the answer, of building a relationship based on curiosity and interest in the other person." In this seminal work he explores the concept of humility, looks at how Humble Inquiry differs from other kinds of inquiry, offers examples of Humble Inquiry in action in many different settings, and shows how to overcome the cultural, organizational and psychological barriers that keep us from practicing it. This is a major new contribution to how we see human dynamics and relationships, presented in a compact, personal, eminently practical way"--

"From one of the true giants in organizational development, career development and organizational psychology comes a simple and effective technique for building more positive relationships--particularly between people of different status--that will lead to more honest and open interactions and stronger organizations"--

pages.text:
Edgar H. Schein examines what changes when a conversation begins with genuine curiosity instead of advice or assumptions. He argues that asking questions whose answers are not already known can create more open relationships, especially when differences in rank make it difficult for people to speak freely.

This first edition explores humility, different forms of inquiry and the cultural habits that encourage telling rather than listening. Examples from professional and personal settings connect the argument to everyday interactions, with particular attention to trust and the exchange of important information.

pages.text:
Tressie McMillan Cottom brings sociological analysis and personal experience together in eight essays about beauty, media, money and power. Her position as a Black woman from the American South informs questions about whose knowledge is recognised and whose experiences are treated as marginal.

The collection moves between the body, public debate and institutions, showing how apparently private judgments can carry wider social consequences. Cottom’s essays invite readers to examine the standards through which people are valued and the unequal authority given to different voices.
